title: Grateful Dead Live at Curtis Hixon Convention Hall on 1973-12-19
source: Matrix from sources: soundboard:  97361; and Dan McDonald's audience tape (new flat transfer)

ai_review.summary: A gorgeous matrix recording captures a high‑energy late‑1973 show highlighted by an epic Here Comes Sunshine and a massive Other One jam.
ai_review.review: The Dusborne/Droncit matrix source delivers crystal‑clear production that lets the band’s powerhouse performance shine. Highlights include a flawless Here Comes Sunshine, a blistering He’s Gone > Truckin’ > The Other One sequence, and soaring slide work on Row Jimmy, while a few slower numbers like Sugaree and Candyman feel sluggish. Overall the show is vibrant and memorable despite minor setlist unevenness.

ai_rating.rationale: Three detailed reviews average 4.67 stars; reviewers praise both musical performance and recording quality, with only occasional song‑level critiques.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Gorgeous production praised by multiple reviewers; matrix provides completeness and clarity, though one reviewer notes the soundboard mix is even clearer.

standout_songs: He’s Gone > Truckin’ > The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set mixes solid rockers with a few mid‑tempo missteps; second set builds into an extended jam suite that dominates the show's momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Delivers soaring wah‑heavy solo on Candyman, crisp slide guitar on Row Jimmy, and magical phrasing on Stella Blue; occasional critique of solo focus but overall strong.
band_member_comments.Phil: Shows experimental side with a noisy bass jam and the Decon Jam; low‑frequency explosions add power to Ramble On Rose and other jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Provides inspired vocal moments (e.g., The Other One) and solid rhythm work, though his vocals on Around and Around are critiqued as over‑the‑top.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith hammers prickly chords, adds bluesy tritone stingers on Big River, and drives the harmonic texture throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s snare shines on Big Railroad Blues and Big River, anchoring the band’s high‑energy moments.
